title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
author: Herman Melville
modernization_rationale: Melville's 1851 prose is dense with archaic diction, biblical cadence, and 19th-century maritime jargon; light modernization of obsolete vocabulary and sentence untangling aids comprehension while preserving the signature voice.

segments.notes: This is the novel's overture; compression should be light on voice and imagery, heavier on the middle landscape-painting/Saco-valley and Tennessee-poet passages if budget forces cuts. Preserve the opening sentence verbatim, the Narcissus key verbatim, and the closing 'snow hill in the air' image verbatim. Retain the playbill's three-line typographic form. Keep the rhetorical-question cascades (Why did the old Persians... Why did the Greeks...) in at least abbreviated form — their cumulative pressure is the voice. Retain 'Who ain't a slave?' as direct quotation. The Cato/pistol-and-ball line and 'damp, drizzly November in my soul' are both culturally famous and should survive as near-verbatim. Modernize L2 only lightly here; Ishmael's periodic sentences are themselves the signature.

plan_notes: This is an unusually long, structurally heterogeneous novel of ~177k words mixing narrative, soliloquy (often in explicit play-script form), sermon, cetological encyclopedia, and embedded novella. The 4.24x compression ratio is aggressive given the amount of signature material that must be preserved. Strategy: compress digressive cetology chapters (32, 55-57, 74-77, 79-80, 82-83, 86, 92, 101-105) very hard — often to a sentence or paragraph — to free budget for signature narrative and voice chapters (1, 9, 23, 36, 41-42, 54, 93-96, 99, 132-135). The framing of cetology as 'draught of a draught' (ch. 32) should itself be preserved; the drafter may occasionally use a bridging sentence like 'Ishmael now digresses on [topic]; his chief point is...' to honor the encyclopedic impulse without reproducing it. Voice: preserve the Ishmael narrator's grandiloquent-ironic register — rhetorical questions, second-person address, biblical cadence, Shakespearean pastiche. When modernizing, lean toward L2: retain archaic 'thee/thou' in Ahab's and Mapple's speech (these are ritual registers) but modernize obscure vocabulary and untangle long Latinate periodic sentences elsewhere. Difficult passages: (a) Fleece's dialect sermon — preserve the rhetorical arc and flavor but normalize the most opaque eye-dialect; (b) Jonah sermon's long Cadiz/Tarshish geography — can trim; (c) Town-Ho's Story frame with Lima dons — preserve the frame compactly and the core Steelkilt narrative; (d) Pip chapters must not be cut or softened — Pip is load-bearing. The Shakespearean soliloquy quartet (37-40) should be preserved as interior-monologue set pieces, format retained. The ending (segments 63+, not shown in this source excerpt which cuts off at ch. 108) will include The Symphony, The Chase (three days), and Epilogue — these are absolute signature material and will receive the lowest compression. Note: source text provided here terminates mid-chapter 108; the plan above covers the segmentation through that point, but downstream stages must continue segmenting chapters 109-135 + Epilogue at similarly signature-weighted compressions. The Epilogue ('And I only am escaped alone to tell thee') must be preserved verbatim.
